subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` lifecycle phases for sub-agent startup, and should that be implemented by replacing the stale candidate branch with a fresh current-main patch?
rationale: The source-level problem is real, but the proposed solution creates a new core lifecycle/API contract that affects gateway waits, session state projection, SDK normalization, and subagent consumers.

options.title: Approve a fresh lifecycle contract
options.body: Implement the two additive phases against the active embedded-agent, subagent registry, gateway wait, session projection, SDK, docs, and focused regression surfaces.

options.title: Narrow to diagnostics only
options.body: Improve logs/status around aborted startup without adding new lifecycle phases, reducing API risk but leaving less precise parent-run semantics.

options.title: Reject the core API change
options.body: Close or narrow the request and rely on external watchdogs or existing timeout behavior for startup-silence detection.

recommendation.title: Approve a fresh lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Implement the two additive phases against the active embedded-agent, subagent registry, gateway wait, session projection, SDK, docs, and focused regression surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant current-main history points to subagent lifecycle and terminal outcome ownership, and this decision crosses those boundaries.
